biblical_reference.note: Stephanus is a common name in the New Testament, occurring more than 20 times. It is derived from the Greek word 'Stephanos', which means 'crown' or 'wreath'. In the Bible, Stephanus is the name of several individuals, including one of the seven deacons in the early Christian church (Acts 6:5, Acts 6:8, Acts 6:15, Acts 7:58, Acts 8:5, Acts 8:29, Acts 9:21, Acts 11:20, Acts 15:35, Acts 26:26), and the author of the Epistle of James (James 1:1).

saint_reference.note: Stephanus of Constantinople was a bishop of Constantinople in the 5th century AD. He was known for his defense of orthodox Christianity against the Nestorian heresy. He is commemorated on April 16 in the Eastern Orthodox Church.
